statement: Insufficient grip force causes MISSED_GRASP and SLIPPED_ON_LIFT failures, especially for heavy cubes and low friction.
mechanism: The normal force from grip_force generates friction to resist gravity and inertial loads. When mass is high and friction is low, the current grip_force (15 N) is too low to prevent slip or missed grasp.
prediction: Increasing grip_force will reduce MISSED_GRASP and SLIPPED_ON_LIFT failure rates in the high-mass, low-friction region (E43), and marginally across all mass and friction bins (E3-E7, E8-E12).

statement: Insufficient grasp_hold_steps after gripper delay causes MISSED_GRASP, especially for small cubes and long gripper delays.
mechanism: The gripper_delay_steps delays the close command; if grasp_hold_steps is too short, the fingers have not fully closed or stabilized before lift begins, causing the cube to be missed. Small cubes are more sensitive to timing.
prediction: Increasing grasp_hold_steps will reduce MISSED_GRASP failures in the small-size, high-delay region (E38) and in high gripper_delay_steps bins (E36, E37).

statement: High sensor noise causes MISSED_GRASP due to misperception of cube position; retries would allow re-perception and reduce these failures.
mechanism: Sensor noise perturbs the perceived cube position, causing the grasp to miss or land on the cube. With retry_count=0, there is no second chance. Increasing retry_count allows a fresh perception attempt.
prediction: Increasing retry_count to at least 1 will reduce MISSED_GRASP failures in high sensor noise regions (E28-E32), especially where sensor noise interacts with small size (E39) or low friction (E41).
